questions.question:
One word substitution for:

A system in which two or more states, groups, or principles coexist.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Pluralism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Pluralism"** refers to a system or condition in which multiple groups, states, or principles coexist while maintaining their distinct identities. (बहुलवाद)
 
 
• **Example:** The nation thrives on its cultural pluralism, where people from diverse backgrounds live harmoniously.
 
 
• The term is often used in political, social, or cultural contexts to describe a state of coexistence and acceptance of diversity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Pluralism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Plurality** (बहुसंख्या): Refers to the state of being numerous or having multiple components. It is also used in elections to describe the number of votes cast for a candidate who receives more than any other but does not receive an absolute majority.
 
 
• **Example:** The candidate won the election by a plurality of votes.
 
 

 
• **Pluralist** (बहुलतावादी): Refers to a person or philosophy that supports or advocates pluralism.
 
 
• **Example:** He is a pluralist who believes in the coexistence of different cultures and religions.
 
 

 
• **Pluralistic** (बहुलतावादी प्रणाली): Describes a system or society that is based on or advocates pluralism.
 
 
• **Example:** The pluralistic nature of the society allows diverse opinions to be expressed freely.

questions.question:
One word substitution for:

A wordy expression or a religious/philosophical emphasis on words rather than the spirit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Verbalism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Verbalism"** refers to a focus on the choice of words or verbal expression rather than the actual meaning or essence. It can also mean the excessive use of words or expressions without much substance. (शब्दाडंबर)
 
 
• **Example:** His speech was full of verbalism, lacking any real solutions to the problem.
 
 
• In the context of the question, "Verbalism" represents a wordy expression or emphasis on words rather than spirit, making it the correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. Verbalism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Verbosity** (शब्दबहुलता): The quality of using more words than needed; wordiness.
 
 
• **Example:** The professor's verbosity made his lecture difficult to follow.
 
 
 
• **Verbiage** (शब्दों की अधिकता): Excessive or meaningless use of words, often in writing or speech.
 
 
• **Example:** The contract was full of legal verbiage that confused the client.
 
 
 
• **Verbalization** (मौखिक अभिव्यक्ति): The act of expressing ideas, feelings, or thoughts in words.
 
 
• **Example:** Her verbalization of her emotions helped her therapist understand her better.
